intelligence.human_view: Think of joining a town, not signing up for a tool. The town hands you a deed written in words you actually use, one piece at a time, with a little eye beside any hard word that explains it. You're a citizen and a representative of the place — not a customer, not a salesperson. The town runs on one road system that connects everything: your notes, your pages, your people, your earnings — all on the same chain, built from the same good parts. It's a master workshop with shelves of perfect parts, each made once, made right: you never whittle a copy of a part when the real one is on the shelf; you take it down and fit it. It's a theatre where the play is one story told the same way every night, but the stage reacts to the audience — and the manager doesn't judge the show by checking that the script printed correctly; she sits in a seat and watches it. And it's a grand hotel that opens room by room as you walk — but if the front door's key doesn't turn, the hotel is not open, no matter how perfect the ballroom is.
intelligence.simple_view: When you join, you get a special paper called a deed. It says: you belong here. Your job is to show people this place, because it's so good it shows itself. The paper opens a little bit at a time. If a word is too hard, there's a tiny eye you can tap. It explains it in easy words. In this workshop, all the pieces are already made and they're beautiful. Your job is to pick the real piece off the shelf. Not to draw a picture of it and pretend. All the buttons in this place match, like a set of shiny buttons on one coat. There's ONE play button that reads the whole story out loud. Our pages open like a storybook. Tap, and the next part unfolds. If the front door key doesn't work, the house is NOT ready. Even if the kitchen is perfect. Being smart isn't being strong or fast or knowing lots of facts. Being smart is DOING the smartest thing. Hurting someone is never the smart thing. It scores zero, every time.
intelligence.grandma_view: A deed used to mean something, dear — it said the land was yours and you belonged to the place. This one says the same, and sensibly: it doesn't bury you in lawyer words, it opens a page at a time and explains itself as it goes. Good houses run this way, dear. You keep a drawer of proper tools and you use them; you don't whittle a spoon every time you need to stir. A repair that only covers the crack will crack again — you fix the wall. Prices come from the ledger, not from a guess. And a cook doesn't serve a dish because the recipe was followed; she tastes it. Machinery can tell you the oven reached temperature. Only the eye and the tongue can tell you it's ready to serve. We always knew this, dear. The clever lad with quick hands who leaves a mess isn't the intelligent one; the one who thinks, chooses well, does the job right and can show you the finished work — that's intelligence.
intelligence.naya_view: Assert the ambassador definition (representative, part of it) wherever the deed or walk describes the role. Verify the deed unfolds on tap with an eye-definition for every hard word. Check every note surface for + CREATE SPACE. Treat "block it in" as an immediate system write, never a note-to-self. Diff every built element against its Factory source; reject restyles and look-alikes. Require structural fixes with the defect class named. Verify ladder numbers against his settled numbers, never a model's guess. Prove each Smart Link join with a real click and a summing count. Reuse the existing button and icon sets; refuse new variants. Assert one play control per agreement surface. Run the eye pass at real widths on the rendered surface and record PASS/FAIL per element; a bytes-only pass is recorded as NOT WHOLE. Verify routing against live membership state, not assumptions. Record bake and live verdicts in separate fields and never merge them into one PASS. Scan citizen-facing copy for backstage phrasing before it ships. Audit every money display for the joins-only rule. Bind every claim to a rendered-page measurement. Test the door leg (sign-in code path) before scoring any membership build. Score the whole surface and log hole-hunting on the most beautiful elements first. Check every finished item exists on the One List; a missing item is a defect with an owner. Brief the ultimate want explicitly in every round and test the result against it, not only against the words. Verify certificates at his viewport width as well as standard widths. Rewrite mirrored copy into stranger-perspective value statements before it ships.
